decision: The track scale is a yard track Scale at South Yard with move count 500
reason: Operations Pro has no scale; a yard track used last keeps it on the switch list without attracting set outs
reverse: Delete the track; move the scale test car

decision: The engine terminal is three Diesel-only yard tracks EH-1..3 inside South Yard, not a separate location
reason: CK1 and the yardmaster are at South Yard; a separate location would need a route stop

decision: One Operations location per island industry, not one "Neville Island" location
reason: The crew documents and Route 23 timetable treat them as stations; colour blocks are per industry
reverse: Merge later; the schedule lines move with the tracks

decision: Industry spur length is 60 ft per STS spot; Off Spot and Storage are alternates of 60 ft
reason: The East End tracks have no measured length in block_lengths.csv; 60 ft fits one 50 ft car with couplers

decision: Scully and Demmler are interchange tracks, not staging
reason: D749 passes through Demmler mid-turn; staging cannot be a middle stop
reverse: Rebuild with staging and split D749

decision: The offline world is one spur per side (POHC Offline, CSX Offline) with a match-mode schedule, 2000 ft, virtual
reason: Deterministic, editable one line per STS shipment, no departure-must-leave rule

decision: North Yard and East Yard are not built
reason: No cars, no measured tracks, STS calls East Yard reserved; CK1's crew card starts at South Yard

decision: D749 is one train, West Yard → South Yard → Demmler Yard → West Yard
reason: The crew card describes one turn; the inbound block picked up at Demmler ties down at West Yard
reverse: Fallback if the three-train route fails in stage 4: D749 built at session end from Demmler, tying down at West Yard, with the block set out at South Yard next session

decision: K-1 and K-2 are pulled by CK1 only; NVL may set out there
reason: STS gives coke pulls to CK1 and lets NVL deliver

decision: STG-SCULLY and STG-DEMMLER stay as trains with no engine, built and terminated by the automation at session end
reason: They are the offline swap STS runs between sessions

decision: Per-step pick-up criteria are replaced by the router with car routing via yards on, and interchange train lists
reason: No per-stop destination filter exists
reverse: Nothing to reverse; it is the program

decision: STS shipments became schedule lines; 84 offline and 28 island lines
reason: One line per shipment keeps the owner's editing surface

decision: Chemicals keep their real names as loads and are flagged hazardous; the general "Process Chemicals" code is not a load
reason: The waybills name them and the seed config carries placards

decision: Two open hopper types: Hopper (coal, aggregate) and Coke Hopper (the 16 coke-fleet cars from the seed config)
reason: Keeps coal cars off the coke ovens and coke cars off the coal unload

decision: Rare IX lines carry random 50; island lines none; STS intervals not copied
reason: Balance is tuned by dry runs

decision: Empties return to the side STS names: Aristech and Calgon to McKees Rocks, A. Stucki, Ferrellgas and Kosmos to McKeesport
reason: outbound_empty_return in the seed config

decision: No divisions
reason: The line destinations already say where empties go

decision: No warm start; the start state is the STS session 3 end
reason: The brief names that dump as the source

decision: Two automations: Session with wait steps for the live day, Session Replay that moves and terminates for tests
reason: A wait needs someone at the layout; a dry run needs no one

decision: No train schedule day is active
reason: One session pattern

decision: On-time build mode off
reason: A train built out of order would abort

decision: Track length is scale feet: inches × 87.1 ÷ 12, rounded to 5
reason: JMRI's length unit is feet and cars are entered in scale feet

decision: Every location, track and stop takes all four directions
reason: Direction is not needed as a filter on a loop with turns

decision: The 28 cars STS does not position (passenger cars, cabooses, no-photo freight cars) and HART 1776 are in the roster with no location
reason: No evidence where they stand; the legacy roster left them unplaced too

decision: hold_custom on every industry spur and both offline spurs
reason: Without staging, a full spur would scatter cars onto yards

decision: Offline lines use explicit receive loads, never blank
reason: A car's load alone then decides its side and spur

decision: No caboose or FRED requirement on any train
reason: The crew cards show none

decision: No startup automation
reason: A startup automation runs on every computer that opens the folder

decision: Cars at offline spurs and island spurs are delivered through the schedule, so their load is whatever the next line gives, not the exact STS order
reason: The schedule is the only way to give a car a final destination

decision: NVL's engine is POHC 2091 (crew card), not CWRY 2091 (repository); the ten locomotives get models with lengths and horsepower from public data
reason: The crew card is the owner's latest word

decision: NW 12986 (STS code HC, a covered hopper) starts empty on Scully Interchange, not on the Shenango coke track where STS had it
reason: K-1 takes Coke Hopper only; the STS position looks like a slip
reverse: place_car to any covered hopper spot

decision: Five delivered cars carry a schedule-chosen load that differs from their STS order: CBQ 171856 and BO 133007 Coal, BO 283057 and BO 283069 Steel Coils, RMLI 2018 Plastic Resins
reason: The offline and team-track schedules pick the next load by rotation (D29)

decision: Scully Interchange stays at its physical 890 ft. The stage 4 dry run left UTLX 36299 on POHC Offline for want of room there, because the dry run builds STG-SCULLY before NVL has pulled the interchange; the ordered session in stage 5 is the test
reason: The loop half is a measured length; a longer track or planned pick ups would hide a real capacity limit
reverse: update_track ignore_used_percent or a longer length
